QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_32

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil (SIA) is debating whether to issue 'limited assurance' or 'reasonable assurance' on Bal Vikas Samiti's outcome metrics. Which statement correctly distinguishes the two?

answer.text: Reasonable assurance provides a higher level of confidence and requires more extensive procedures, expressed positively ('in our opinion, the outcomes are fairly presented'); limited assurance provides a lower level, expressed negatively ('nothing has come to our attention that would cause us to believe…')
Limited assurance is higher; reasonable assurance is lower
Both provide identical levels of confidence
Limited assurance is only used for Big Four firms; reasonable for others

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Reasonable assurance = higher level of confidence, more extensive evidence procedures, positive-form opinion ('in our opinion the outcomes are fairly presented in all material respects'). Limited assurance = lower level of confidence, less extensive procedures, negative-form conclusion ('nothing has come to our attention that would cause us to believe…'). This is the global assurance-framework convention reflected in SAS. **The Trap:** Options B, C, D are false. The positive vs negative form of opinion is the distinguishing language cue. **Cross-Exam Context:** III-A / III-C Compliance touch ISAE 3000 reasonable vs limited assurance; XXIII applies the same ladder to SAS-100 SIA engagements. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Set the assurance level in the engagement letter BEFORE field work — upgrading from limited to reasonable mid-engagement is expensive because sample sizes jump materially.
